crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Credit Scoring with Alternative Data
children.blurb: Credit scoring with alternative data extends traditional credit assessment beyond bureau files and application data to sources such as rental payments, utility bills, telecom records, bank transaction flows, e-commerce activity, and small business accounting or point-of-sale data.

children.name: Covenant Extraction
children.blurb: Covenant extraction is the use of natural language processing and machine learning to identify, classify, and structure the contractual terms in bond indentures and loan agreements.

children.name: Predicting Distress and Default
children.blurb: Predicting distress and default covers models that estimate the probability a corporate or sovereign borrower will miss payments, enter bankruptcy, or restructure, using financial statements, market prices, news, and alternative data.

children.name: Modelling the Yield Curve
children.blurb: Yield curve modelling in fixed income and credit risk concerns the term structure of interest rates across maturities, from overnight to long dated government and credit instruments.

children.name: Stress Testing Structured Credit
children.blurb: Stress testing structured credit means assessing how tranches of securitized products such as CLOs, ABS, RMBS, and CMBS would perform under severe economic and market shocks, including defaults, prepayments, spread widening, and rating migration.

sections.body: Fixed income and credit risk is the work of estimating whether borrowers will pay, how bond prices reflect that risk, and how portfolios behave under stress. AI now reads loan files, earnings calls, transaction records, and news to build credit scores from alternative data, not just traditional bureau files. Natural language processing pulls covenants and terms out of dense credit agreements so analysts can compare protections across issuers. Machine learning models combine market prices, accounting ratios, and payment histories to flag early signs of distress and default. For the yield curve, statistical and neural methods fit term structures, interpolate missing maturities, and test how shocks move rates. In structured credit, simulation and ML-assisted scenario engines stress tranches, collateral pools, and cash flow waterfalls under many economic paths.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, like using gradient boosting and logistic regression for credit scoring, where gains over traditional scorecards are real but often modest. Covenant extraction has improved with large language models, yet long documents, unusual clauses, and cross references still cause errors that require human review. Distress prediction works better as a ranking tool than as a precise probability, and it struggles when regimes change or data is sparse. Yield curve modeling is well understood, but AI adds most value in fitting rich data sets and handling liquidity gaps, not in replacing no-arbitrage finance. Stress testing structured credit remains hard because correlations, prepayments, and legal structures interact in ways models approximate poorly. Honest limits include data bias, opaque model behavior, regulatory scrutiny, and the fact that a model cannot invent information that was never recorded.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a chain from individual credit assessment to portfolio level risk. Credit Scoring with Alternative Data explains how new data sources enter borrower evaluation and where fairness questions arise. Covenant Extraction covers the document parsing work that turns legal language into structured terms for monitoring and enforcement. Predicting Distress and Default connects those borrower signals to early warning systems and default models. Modelling the Yield Curve provides the discounting and rate framework that prices fixed income cash flows and supports relative value analysis. Stress Testing Structured Credit takes all of these inputs and asks how tranches, pools, and waterfalls behave under adverse scenarios.
